# @netforge/engine-sim (llms-full.txt)

> The full reference for the deterministic shared simulation of the Net Forge game engine: the same TypeScript module runs client prediction in the browser and authority on a room server. Part 1 is the summary (llms.txt). Part 2 is the behaviour reference: ticks, inputs, snapshots, rendering, determinism, content, arena, physics, platform and kart modes. Parts 3 to 5 are the public source: the package's export list, the core types (src/api.ts) and the physics types (src/physics/types.ts), with their doc comments.

## Part 1: summary

### Install

- `npm install @netforge/engine-sim` (Node 20 or later, or a modern browser)
- Call `await initSim()` once per process before anything else (it loads the Rapier WASM).

### Core loop

- `createWorld(config)` builds a world (`tickRate`, `seed`, `enemies`, `content`, ...); `destroyWorld(world)` frees it.
- `addPlayer(world, id)` and `removePlayer(world, id)`.
- `step(world, inputs)` advances one fixed tick. `inputs` is a `Map<PlayerId, InputCommand>`; `InputCommand` is `{ seq, tick, moveX, moveZ, yaw, buttons }` with `Button` bits. It returns `{ tick, events }` and never reads a clock.
- `FixedStepper` converts wall-clock time into ticks plus a render `alpha`.
- `quantizeInput`, `encodeInput` (15 bytes), `decodeInput`, `encodeInputs`, `decodeInputs`.
- `captureState(world, include?)`, `applyState(world, state)`, `encodeSnapshot(state, baseline?)`, `decodeSnapshot(bytes, baseline)`, `snapshotBaseTick(bytes)`.
- `renderView(world)`: typed arrays of current and previous-tick poses for interpolation.
- `playerNetId`, `lastProcessedSeq` (the ack that client reconciliation keys on).

### Modes

- Content mode (horde games): `content.weapons`, `content.enemyTypes`, `content.stats`; `spawnEnemy`, `resetRun`, `respawnDead`, `revivePlayer`, `listPlayers`, `enemyCount`, `grantUpgrade`, `setCosmetic`, `simRandom`.
- Arena mode (`content.arena.enabled`): twin-stick, loadouts, PvP, respawns; lag compensation through `beamShot`, `arenaHitboxes`, `applyBeamHit`.
- Platform mode: `createPlatformWorld`, `platformStep`, `capturePlatformPlayer`, `applyPlatformPlayer`.
- Kart mode: `createKartWorld`, `kartStep`, `captureKart`, `applyKart`.

### Physics

- `createPhysics({ tickRate, gravity })` returns a `PhysicsWorld`; `restorePhysics(bytes)` rebuilds one from `snapshot()`.
- Bodies: `addBody`, `addStaticBox`, `addTrigger`, `addCharacter`, `addJoint`, `removeBody`, `setKinematicTarget`, `applyImpulse`, `applyForce`, `applyKnockback`.
- Layers: `Layer`, `layerMask`, `ALL_LAYERS`. Two bodies touch only when each mask holds the other's layer.
- Queries: `raycast`, `raycastAll`, `shapeCast`, `overlap`.
- `step(inputs)` returns `{ tick, events, characters }`; events are `contact.start`, `contact.end`, `trigger.enter`, `trigger.exit`, sorted.
- `stateHash()` and `snapshotHash()` for determinism checks; `destroy()` frees the WASM memory.

### Rules

- Never read clocks or `Math.random` inside the simulation; use the world seed and `simRandom`.
- Quantize inputs on both sides (`step` does it on entry).
- The server is authoritative; clients predict their own player and reconcile from snapshots.

### Docs

- llms-full.txt in this package: the full reference with every public type and its doc comments.
- https://forge.netnet.capital/docs/packages/engine-sim
- Related packages: @netforge/engine (the game API and runtime), @netforge/kit-play (run a game locally).

## Part 2: behaviour reference

### Public API

Everything is exported from the package root. Types live in `src/api.ts`.

```ts
import {
  initSim, createWorld, destroyWorld, addPlayer, removePlayer, step,
  quantizeInput, encodeInput, decodeInput, encodeInputs, decodeInputs,
  captureState, applyState, encodeSnapshot, decodeSnapshot, snapshotBaseTick,
  renderView, playerNetId, lastProcessedSeq, FixedStepper,
  Button, EntityKind, DEFAULT_TICK_RATE,
} from "@netforge/engine-sim";

await initSim();                         // once per process (Rapier WASM)
const world = createWorld({ tickRate: 30, seed: 7, enemies: { target: 2000 } });
addPlayer(world, 1);

// THE API: one fixed tick, all players' inputs for that tick.
const { tick, events } = step(world, new Map([[1, { seq: 1, tick: 0, moveX: 0, moveZ: 1, yaw: 0, buttons: Button.Fire }]]));
```

#### Ticks

- `step(world, inputs)` advances exactly one fixed tick of `1 / tickRate`
  seconds. It never reads a clock. Systems run in a fixed order: input,
  AI, physics, combat, pickups, spawners, game rules, lifetime.
- `FixedStepper` turns wall-clock deltas into a tick count plus a render
  `alpha`. It is clock-free too, so the client drives it from
  `requestAnimationFrame` and the server from its own loop.

#### Inputs

- `InputCommand { seq, tick, moveX, moveZ, yaw, buttons }`. `seq` increases
  per player; `step` records the last consumed `seq` as that player's `ack`
  in the state, which is what client reconciliation keys on.
- Every command is quantized on entry (`quantizeInput`: moves to 1/127, yaw
  to a u16 turn), so the predicting client and the authoritative server
  consume bit-identical inputs.
- `encodeInput` is 15 bytes. `encodeInputs` packs several (send the last
  few unacked commands in every packet to ride out loss).
- A player missing from `inputs` gets a neutral command for that tick.

#### State and snapshots

- `captureState(world, include?)` returns a `SimState`: integers only
  (positions and velocities in 1/1024 m fixed point, yaw as a u16 turn),
  entities sorted by `netId`. `include` is the interest-management hook:
  pass a filter per client.
- The sim snaps its own state onto that grid at the end of every tick, so
  `applyState(world, captureState(other))` reproduces `other` exactly and
  both worlds keep stepping identically.
- `encodeSnapshot(state)` is a full snapshot; `encodeSnapshot(state, baseline)`
  is a delta against a state the receiver already acknowledged. Fields are
  zigzag varints of the difference from the baseline (a full snapshot is a
  delta against nothing), with a per-entity changed-field mask, so a resting
  entity costs about 3 bytes and a walking one about 8.
- `snapshotBaseTick(bytes)` tells the receiver which baseline a delta needs;
  `decodeSnapshot(bytes, baseline)` throws if the wrong one is passed.

#### Rendering

`renderView(world)` returns dense typed arrays (`netId`, `kind`, `x/y/z`,
`yaw`, and `prevX/prevY/prevZ/prevYaw` from the previous tick) so the
renderer interpolates with the stepper's `alpha` without touching the ECS.

### Determinism

Practical: the same module and the same Rapier
build (`@dimforge/rapier3d-deterministic-compat`, cross-platform
determinism enabled) on both sides, entity iteration in `netId` order, a
seeded PRNG in the state, and state quantized every tick. On one engine
the same inputs give the same snapshot bytes (tested over 1,000 ticks).
Across JavaScript engines `Math.sin/cos` may differ in the last bit; the
server is authoritative and clients reconcile, so that is acceptable.

### The default world (no content)

A walled square arena with cylindrical pillars (`DEFAULT_ARENA`), player
characters on Rapier's kinematic character controller (walk, sprint, jump
with coyote time and a jump buffer, Fire = radial pulse), and an enemy
spawner that keeps `enemies.target` chasers alive on a ring around the
players. Enemies steer in the ECS (seek the nearest player, separate from
neighbours on a uniform grid, slide off pillars and players); they are not
Rapier bodies, which keeps 2,000 of them at about 2.5-3.5 ms a tick in
Node on a laptop. Navmesh steering (`recast-navigation-js`) replaces the
seek when templates need it.


### Content mode (horde games)

When the config lists `content.weapons`, the world runs the genre
machinery templates build on instead of the arena rules above:

- **Enemy types** (`content.enemyTypes`): health, speed, radius, contact
  damage, XP, boss, mass. `spawnEnemy(world, type, x, z)` spawns one; the
  game runner in @netforge/engine drives waves.
- **Weapons fire by themselves**: `nova` (hits everything in range when an
  enemy is near), `bolt` (projectiles at the nearest enemy, piercing),
  `orbit` (blades circling the player, `orbitAngle` is exported so
  renderers draw them where the sim hits). Level scaling: +25% damage a
  level, an extra projectile or blade every second level, -6% cooldown.
- **XP gems** drop from kills (capped by `progression.maxPickups`; past it
  XP goes straight to the killer) and are pulled in by a magnet radius.
- **Level-ups** offer three upgrades (`choices` field) drawn from a hash of
  (seed, netId, level), not the world PRNG, so a predicting client agrees
  with the server. `Button.Choice1..3` take one.
- **Passives** (`content.stats`): speed, maxHealth, magnet, might, haste,
  regen, armor.
- **Co-op downed and revive**: at zero health a player is downed and bleeds
  out; a teammate standing within `coop.reviveRadius` revives them; bled-out
  players are out until `respawnDead`. `revivePlayer` is the paid revive.
- **Dash** on `Button.Sprint` with invulnerability and an input buffer
  (`coop.dashBufferTicks`): a press just before the cooldown ends still dashes.
- **Corpses**: a killed enemy keeps its NetId for `coop.corpseTicks` with
  `EntityFlag.Dead`, so clients see it die instead of vanish.
- Run control: `resetRun`, `listPlayers`, `enemyCount`, `entityHealth`,
  `setCosmetic`, `spawnRingPoint`, `simRandom`.

Snapshot version 2 carries the new per-entity fields. Determinism, capture
and apply in content mode are tested (`test/content.test.ts`); the bench
reports 4 players and 2,000 enemies at about 1.5 ms a tick.

### Arena mode (the arena shooter)

`content.arena.enabled` turns content mode into the arena shooter's
machinery (src/arena.ts), on the same fields and snapshot format:

- **Twin-stick**: `moveX`/`moveZ` move in the world frame, `yaw` is the aim.
- **Loadouts** (`progression.loadout`, up to 4 weapons in the packed
  `weapons` slots; the selected slot rides in `choices & 3`).
  `Button.Choice1..3` pick a slot, `Button.Alt` cycles, `Button.Fire`
  fires the selected weapon when its cooldown is ready: `blaster`
  (projectiles fanned over `spread`, swept against players so nothing
  tunnels, stopped by pillars), `beam` (hitscan, clamped by pillars and
  walls with `beamRange`), `nova` (a blast around you).
- **PvP**: players hurt each other (no self damage); at zero health a
  player is killed (`player.killed` with `by`), drops a heal pickup, waits
  `arena.respawnTicks` and respawns at the spawn point farthest from every
  opponent (`arenaSpawn`) with `arena.spawnIframeTicks` of protection that
  firing ends.
- **Authority**: `arena.authority` is false on a predicting client, which
  then predicts only its own movement, aim, weapon choice and cooldowns
  (no projectiles, hits or respawns of its own).
- **Lag compensation seam**: with `arena.externalHitscan` (room servers),
  human beams are not resolved in `step`; the room asks `beamShot(world,
  player, cmd)` before the step, rewinds `arenaHitboxes` to what the
  shooter saw, and applies the hit with `applyBeamHit`. Bots
  (`BOT_PLAYER_BASE` and up) and the headless harness resolve beams in the
  sim against the present.
- Store upgrades: `grantUpgrade(world, player, statIndex)` adds one passive
  level for the rest of the run. `listPickups` feeds bots.

Tested in `test/arena.test.ts`: loadout and slot choice, world-frame
movement, kills and respawn, pillars stopping bolts, beams in the sim and
through the external seam, exact prediction of the shooter's own state,
and snapshot restore mid-fight.

### Physics

`createPhysics()` gives a game real rigid-body physics on the same
deterministic Rapier build, independent of the survivor world above
(`src/physics/`). Everything is keyed by a `BodyId` the wrapper assigns in
creation order and never reuses, every loop runs in BodyId order, and
events come back sorted, so the same calls on two worlds (or on a world
and its restored snapshot) give bit-identical states.

```ts
import { initSim, createPhysics, restorePhysics, Layer, layerMask } from "@netforge/engine-sim";

await initSim();
const phys = createPhysics({ tickRate: 30, gravity: [0, -20, 0] });
phys.addStaticBox([30, 0.5, 30], [0, -0.5, 0]);                 // level, on Layer.Level
const crate = phys.addBody({ type: "dynamic", shape: { box: [0.4, 0.4, 0.4] }, position: [2, 1, 0], mass: 8, restitution: 0.2 });
const zone = phys.addTrigger({ box: [2, 2, 2] }, [8, 1, 0]);      // sensor: enter and exit events only
const hero = phys.addCharacter({ position: [0, 1, 0], dashTicks: 6, coyoteTicks: 5 });

const { events, characters } = phys.step(new Map([[hero, { moveX: 1, moveZ: 0, jump: false, dash: false }]]));
phys.applyKnockback(crate, [0, 0, 0], 6, { lift: 2 });         // 6 m/s away from the blast, 2 m/s up
const hit = phys.raycast([0, 1, 0], [1, 0, 0], 50, { mask: layerMask("Level", "Prop"), exclude: [hero] });
const bytes = phys.snapshot();                                  // reconcile: restorePhysics(bytes)
```

- **Bodies**: `addBody({ type: "dynamic" | "kinematic" | "static", shape, position, rotation, mass | density, friction, restitution, linearDamping, angularDamping, gravityScale, layer, mask, sensor, ccd, lockRotations, linearVelocity, angularVelocity, userData })`,
  `removeBody`, `setPosition`, `setRotation`, `setLinearVelocity`, `setAngularVelocity`, `position`, `rotation`, `velocity`, `angularVelocity`, `mass`,
  `applyImpulse` (N·s), `applyForce` (N, this step only), `applyKnockback(id, from, strength, { lift, byMass })` (a velocity change; `byMass` divides it by mass),
  `setKinematicTarget(id, pos, rot?)` for moving platforms and doors (they push dynamic bodies), `wake`, `sleep`, `isSleeping`.
  Shapes: `{ box: [hx, hy, hz] }`, `{ sphere: r }`, `{ capsule: [halfHeight, r] }`, `{ cylinder: [halfHeight, r] }`. Sugar: `addStaticBox`, `addTrigger`.
- **Layers**: `Layer.Level, Player, Enemy, Projectile, Pickup, Prop, Trigger, Debris, User1..User8` (16 bits). A body is on one layer and has a mask (default every layer). The rule is pairwise, Rapier's: two bodies touch only when EACH one's mask holds the other's layer, so both sides of a pair must agree. Queries look only at the layers in their `mask`.
- **Events** from `step()`: `contact.start`, `contact.end`, `trigger.enter`, `trigger.exit`, each `{ a, b }` with `a < b`, sorted by `(a, b, type)`.
- **Queries**: `raycast` (point, normal, distance), `raycastAll` (nearest first), `shapeCast(shape, from, dir, maxDist)`, `overlap(shape, position)`; options `mask`, `exclude`, `includeSensors`.
- **CCD**: `ccd: true` on fast bodies (bullets, thrown props). Rapier 0.21 also builds speculative contacts from velocity, so plain fast spheres already stop on static walls (tested up to 2,000 m/s); CCD adds the swept pass. Neither fully covers a thin body spinning fast, so keep projectiles round.
- **Joints**: `addJoint({ kind: "fixed" | "ball" | "hinge" | "slider", a, b, anchorA, anchorB, axis })`, `removeJoint`.
- **Character motor** (`addCharacter`): a capsule on Rapier's kinematic character controller with slopes (`maxSlopeClimb`; faces steeper than it are slid down, not stood on), steps (`stepHeight`, `stepWidth`), ground snapping (`snapToGround`), coyote time and jump buffering (ticks), variable jump height (`jumpCut` when jump is released while rising), separate ground and air acceleration (air control), `maxSpeed`, `gravityScale`, `terminalVelocity`, a dash (`dashTicks`, `dashSpeed`, `dashCooldownTicks`, `dashBufferTicks`, optional invulnerability) and pushing dynamic bodies. Input per tick is `{ moveX, moveZ, jump, dash }` in world space with held buttons (edges are found inside). `step()` returns a report per character (`grounded`, `landed`, `jumped`, `dashed`, `hitCeiling`, `groundNormal`); `characterState(id)` and `setCharacterState(id, s)` read and write the whole motor state for reconciliation. Knockback and impulses work on characters too. The default mask includes `Layer.Trigger` so triggers see characters (the motor itself ignores sensors).
- **Snapshots**: `snapshot()` is Rapier's own world snapshot plus the wrapper's ids, characters and joints; `restorePhysics(bytes)` rebuilds it, and stepping both gives the same bits. `stateHash()` hashes the raw float bits of every pose, velocity and motor state in BodyId order (equal hash, identical world); `snapshotHash()` hashes the snapshot bytes.
- `destroy()` frees the WebAssembly memory.

Rapier's scene queries only see colliders after a step, so the wrapper
runs a zero-length step (nothing moves) before a query or a step when
bodies were added, removed or teleported since the last one; that flag
rides in snapshots. Tests: `test/physics.test.ts` and
`test/physics-character.test.ts` (lockstep and replay determinism over 600
ticks, snapshot and restore mid-jump and mid-dash, CCD, layers, triggers,
contacts, ray and shape queries, restitution, friction, knockback, forces,
kinematic pushing, joints, and every motor feature).

### Platform mode (SKYLEDGE, the platformer)

`createPlatformWorld({ tickRate, levels, tuning, statSteps })` and
`platformStep(world, inputs)` (src/platform.ts) run a side-view race to the
flag in pure TypeScript: swept AABB movement against axis-aligned blocks on
a 1/1024 grid, so a predicting client replays its own climber exactly.
Coyote time, a jump buffer, variable jump height, apex hang, fall gravity,
corner nudges, an air dash, one-way ledges, moving platforms on the world
clock, springs, thorns, checkpoints and per-player coins. Climbers are
ghosts to each other. `capturePlatformPlayer` / `applyPlatformPlayer` are
the wire state. Tested in `test/platform.test.ts`.

### Kart mode (TORQUEBAY, the racer)

`createKartWorld({ tickRate, tracks, tuning, statSteps, authority })` and
`kartStep(world, inputs)` (src/kart.ts) run arcade kart physics on closed
tracks (a Catmull-Rom centreline sampled every ~2 m with a width, a grass
verge and barriers): forward and sideways velocity with grip, steering by
speed, drifts that charge a three-tier mini-turbo, boost pads, coins that
raise top speed, laps through ordered quarter checkpoints, and kart bumps
on the authority only (a predicting client leaves them out and the next
snapshot corrects). `captureKart` / `applyKart` are the wire state. Tested
in `test/kart.test.ts` (laps, drift tiers, pads, walls, bumps, upgrades,
exact replay).

## Part 3: exports (src/index.ts)

Everything below is exported from the package root.


## Part 4: core types (src/api.ts)

```ts
/**
 * Public types of @netforge/engine-sim.
 *
 * The sim is the one TypeScript module that runs identically in the browser
 * (client prediction) and on the room server (authority).
 * Everything a caller needs is in this file;
 * the ECS and Rapier internals stay behind `SimWorld`.
 *
 * THE API is `step(world, inputs)`. Around it:
 *   - `initSim()` once per process (loads the Rapier WebAssembly),
 *   - `createWorld(config)` / `destroyWorld(world)`,
 *   - `addPlayer` / `removePlayer`,
 *   - input commands: `quantizeInput`, `encodeInput(s)`, `decodeInput(s)`,
 *   - snapshots: `captureState` → `encodeSnapshot` (full or delta) on the
 *     server, `decodeSnapshot` → `applyState` on the client,
 *   - `renderView(world)` for the renderer (typed arrays, interpolation-ready),
 *   - `FixedStepper` for the fixed-timestep accumulator on either side.
 */

/** A 3-vector in metres, y up. */
export type Vec3 = readonly [x: number, y: number, z: number];

/** A player slot in a room, 1..65535. 0 means "no player". */
export type PlayerId = number;

/**
 * A stable network id for one entity (u32, never reused within a world).
 * 0 means "none". Snapshots are keyed by NetId, never by ECS entity id.
 */
export type NetId = number;

/** Default fixed tick rate in Hz (spec §4: 30 Hz default, 60 for shooters). */
export const DEFAULT_TICK_RATE = 30;

/** Snapshot wire format version (first byte after the magic). */
export const SNAPSHOT_VERSION = 2;

/** Fixed-point units per metre for positions in state and snapshots. */
export const POSITION_SCALE = 1024;
/** Fixed-point units per metre/second for velocities. */
export const VELOCITY_SCALE = 1024;
/** Yaw is a u16 turn: 65536 units per full revolution. */
export const YAW_UNITS = 65536;

/** Input button bits. Games may use bits 8..15 for their own actions. */
export const Button = {
  Jump: 1 << 0,
  Fire: 1 << 1,
  Alt: 1 << 2,
  Use: 1 << 3,
  /** Sprint in the arena; dash (with a short invulnerability) when content is configured. */
  Sprint: 1 << 4,
  /** Pick upgrade 1, 2 or 3 of a pending level-up (content mode). */
  Choice1: 1 << 5,
  Choice2: 1 << 6,
  Choice3: 1 << 7,
  /** Content mode: reroll the open cards (uses one of the run's rerolls). */
  Reroll: 1 << 8,
  /** Content mode: skip the open cards (a small heal instead). */
  Skip: 1 << 9,
  /** Between runs: ready for the next one (the end screen's "Play again" vote). */
  Ready: 1 << 10,
} as const;
export type ButtonBit = (typeof Button)[keyof typeof Button];

/**
 * Keeper (character) choice rides input bits 11..14 as index + 1 (0: no
 * choice). It is held, not pressed: the sim takes it while the keeper is
 * still level 1 with nothing pending (the start of a run), so a client
 * keeps sending its pick and it lands on the first tick of every run.
 */
export const KEEPER_SHIFT = 11;
export const KEEPER_MASK = 0xf << KEEPER_SHIFT;
/** Input bits that choose keeper `index` (0..14). */
export const keeperButtons = (index: number): number => (((index + 1) & 0xf) << KEEPER_SHIFT) >>> 0;

/**
 * A playable character: its start weapon and a signature passive at level 1.
 * Clients draw it from its index (Player `value` bits 12..15).
 */
export interface CharacterDef {
  /** Weapon index the keeper starts every run with. */
  readonly weapon: number;
  /** Passive stat index it starts at level 1 (-1: none). */
  readonly stat: number;
}

/** How a gem's XP is shared in co-op. */
export interface XpShare {
  /** "collector": the collector only. "nearby": `fraction` to every other living player within `radius` m. "all": the full amount to everyone up. */
  readonly mode: "collector" | "nearby" | "all";
  readonly fraction: number;
  readonly radius: number;
}

/** Entity kinds carried in snapshots. */
export const EntityKind = {
  Player: 1,
  Enemy: 2,
  Projectile: 3,
  Pickup: 4,
} as const;
export type EntityKindId = (typeof EntityKind)[keyof typeof EntityKind];

/** Per-entity state flag bits (EntityState.flags). */
export const EntityFlag = {
  Grounded: 1 << 0,
  /** Players: dead (arena: respawning; co-op: out until `respawnDead`). Enemies: a corpse, removed after `coop.corpseTicks`. */
  Dead: 1 << 1,
  /** Players in co-op: downed, bleeding out, can be revived by a teammate. */
  Downed: 1 << 2,
  /** Players: dashing (invulnerable). */
  Dashing: 1 << 3,
  /**
   * Players: the only player in the room (set by the authority from the
   * true player count). Solo upgrade cards pause the sim; co-op cards shove
   * enemies back instead. Predicting clients read it, never count players.
   */
  Solo: 1 << 4,
  /** Enemies: carrying a shield (a shielder's gift); hits drain the shield first. */
  Shielded: 1 << 5,
  /** Enemies: an elite (bigger, tougher, gold rim). Projectiles: a ground hazard (it does not move; it lands when its timer ends). */
  Elite: 1 << 6,
  /** Projectiles: hostile (an enemy's shot or hazard; it hurts players, never enemies). */
  Hostile: 1 << 7,
} as const;

/**
 * One player's input for one tick. Serializable and sequence-numbered.
 *
 * The sim quantizes every command on entry (`quantizeInput`), so a client's
 * prediction and the server's authority consume bit-identical inputs.
 * Wire size: 15 bytes (`INPUT_BYTES`).
 */
export interface InputCommand {
  /** Client sequence number, strictly increasing per player (u32). */
  seq: number;
  /** The sim tick the client produced this for (u32). Informational: `step` does not reject a mismatch. */
  tick: number;
  /** Strafe right (+) / left (-), -1..1 in the character's frame. Quantized to 1/127. */
  moveX: number;
  /** Forward (+) / back (-), -1..1 in the character's frame. Quantized to 1/127. */
  moveZ: number;
  /** Facing in radians about +y (0 faces -z). Quantized to a u16 turn. */
  yaw: number;
  /** Bitmask of `Button` (u16). */
  buttons: number;
}

/** Bytes per encoded InputCommand. */
export const INPUT_BYTES = 15;

/**
 * The inputs for one tick, by player. A player with no entry this tick gets
 * a neutral input (no move, no buttons, facing kept). A room server that
 * wants "repeat last input on packet loss" passes the repeat explicitly.
 */
export type TickInputs = ReadonlyMap<PlayerId, InputCommand>;

/** A cylindrical pillar in the arena (static collider). */
export interface Pillar {
  readonly x: number;
  readonly z: number;
  readonly radius: number;
  readonly height: number;
}

/**
 * An axis-aligned box standing on the floor, `wallHeight` tall: a dungeon's
 * walls. Centre (x, z) and half sizes hx, hz in metres.
 */
export interface WallBox {
  readonly x: number;
  readonly z: number;
  readonly hx: number;
  readonly hz: number;
}

/** The static level. Part of the world's config, never of a snapshot. */
export interface ArenaConfig {
  /** The floor is a square from -halfExtent to +halfExtent on x and z (m). */
  readonly halfExtent: number;
  readonly wallHeight: number;
  readonly pillars: readonly Pillar[];
  /**
   * Wall boxes inside the square (a dungeon). Players collide with them in
   * physics; enemies and bolts are resolved against them like pillars.
   */
  readonly walls?: readonly WallBox[];
  /**
   * Walkable floor rectangles (rooms and corridors). When present, only
   * these are ground: spawns land on them, and enemies path between them
   * on a flow field instead of running straight at a player behind a wall.
   */
  readonly floors?: readonly WallBox[];
  /** Where players spawn and respawn. */
  readonly spawn: Vec3;
}

export interface PlayerRules {
  /** Ground speed, m/s. */
  readonly speed: number;
  /** Sprint multiplier while Button.Sprint is held. */
  readonly sprintMultiplier: number;
  /** Initial jump velocity, m/s. */
  readonly jumpVelocity: number;
  /** Gravity, m/s² (positive number, applied downward). */
  readonly gravity: number;
  /** Capsule radius and half-height of the cylindrical part, m. */
  readonly radius: number;
  readonly halfHeight: number;
  readonly maxHealth: number;
  /** Fire = radial pulse: radius (m), cooldown (ticks). */
  readonly pulseRadius: number;
  readonly pulseCooldownTicks: number;
  /** Ticks after a jump input during which a landing still jumps (jump buffer). */
  readonly jumpBufferTicks: number;
  /** Ticks after leaving the ground during which a jump still works (coyote time). */
  readonly coyoteTicks: number;
}

export interface EnemyRules {
  /** The spawner keeps this many enemies alive. 0 disables enemies. */
  readonly target: number;
  /** Max enemies spawned per tick while below target. */
  readonly spawnPerTick: number;
  /** Spawn ring distance from the nearest player, m. */
  readonly spawnRadius: number;
  readonly speed: number;
  readonly radius: number;
  readonly maxHealth: number;
  /** Damage per contact, and ticks between contacts from one enemy. */
  readonly contactDamage: number;
  readonly contactCooldownTicks: number;
}

/**
 * One enemy prefab, compiled from the game API (`prefab(...)`). Enemy type
 * 0 is always the arena's `EnemyRules` (the built-in target spawner uses it).
 */
export interface EnemyTypeDef {
  readonly health: number;
  /** m/s. */
  readonly speed: number;
  /** m. */
  readonly radius: number;
  /** Contact damage per touch. */
  readonly damage: number;
  /** XP carried by the gem it drops; 0 drops nothing. */
  readonly xp: number;
  readonly boss?: boolean;
  /** Knockback divisor. Default 1; bosses want 10+. */
  readonly mass?: number;
  /** Behaviour (default "chase"). "idle" stands still. */
  readonly ai?: EnemyAi;
  /** Numbers for the behaviour's attack (defaults per role in roles.ts). */
  readonly attack?: EnemyAttack;
  /** On death, spawn `count` enemies of type `type` where it fell (splitters). */
  readonly split?: { readonly type: number; readonly count: number };
  /** Boss patterns (bosses only): attacks it picks from, the enrage threshold, and the add it summons. */
  readonly pattern?: BossPattern;
  /** Special pickups it may drop: an index into content.pickups and a chance 0..1 (rolled on the sim's PRNG). */
  readonly drops?: readonly { readonly pickup: number; readonly chance: number }[];
  /** A breakable prop (urn, lantern): it never moves, never hurts, and is never recycled. */
  readonly prop?: boolean;
}

/** What a special pickup does when a player collects it. */
export type PickupEffect = "heal" | "vacuum" | "bomb" | "chest";

/**
 * A special pickup (content.pickups). Entities carry PICKUP_SPECIAL + index
 * as their type; gem tiers stay 0..2.
 *  - heal: `amount` of max health (0..1) or hit points (above 1);
 *  - vacuum: every gem on the floor flies to the collector;
 *  - bomb: kills every non-boss enemy on the collector's screen;
 *  - chest: `amount` card picks (1-3; a ready evolution shows first).
 */
export interface PickupTypeDef {
  readonly effect: PickupEffect;
  readonly amount: number;
  /** Chests: a weapon the player holds with its paired passive jumps to max level, so its evolution is on the cards. */
  readonly evolve?: boolean;
}

/** Pickup entity types from here up are special pickups (index = type - PICKUP_SPECIAL). */
export const PICKUP_SPECIAL = 16;

/**
 * Attack numbers for an enemy role. Every field is optional; the role's
 * defaults (roles.ts ROLE_DEFAULTS) fill the rest. Seconds and metres.
 */
export interface EnemyAttack {
  /** Damage of the attack (default: the enemy's contact damage, x1.4 for a blast). */
  readonly damage?: number;
  /** Trigger or keep-away distance, m. */
  readonly range?: number;
  /** Telegraph time before it lands, ticks. */
  readonly windupTicks?: number;
  /** Ticks between attacks. */
  readonly cooldownTicks?: number;
  /** Charge speed multiple, or shot speed m/s. */
  readonly speed?: number;
  /** Blast or aura radius, m. */
  readonly radius?: number;
  /** Summoners: the enemy type index they call. */
  readonly summon?: number;
  /** Summoners: adds per call; support roles: allies affected. */
  readonly count?: number;
}

/** What a boss can do. Each is telegraphed before it lands. */
export type BossAttack = "slam" | "dash" | "leap" | "rain" | "ring" | "fan" | "summon";

export interface BossPattern {
  readonly attacks: readonly BossAttack[];
  /** Health fraction below which the boss enrages (faster, shorter wind-ups, more projectiles). 0 never. */
  readonly enrageAt: number;
  /** Enemy type index `summon` calls (default: type 0). */
  readonly summon?: number;
  /** A mini-boss: its death raises "miniboss.killed", not "boss.killed". */
  readonly mini?: boolean;
}

/** What dealt a hit to a player. Everything but "contact" was telegraphed first. */
export type HitSource = "contact" | "charge" | "blast" | "projectile" | "slam" | "hazard";

/** Enemy behaviours the sim runs (content mode). */
export type EnemyAi =
  | "chase"
  | "idle"
  | "runner"
  | "charger"
  | "ranged"
  | "bomber"
  | "shielder"
  | "healer"
  | "summoner"
  | "flee"
  | "wander";

/**
 * Enemy telegraph word (EntityState.level on enemies and hostile
 * projectiles; it rides snapshots): kind in bits 0-2, fill progress 0..31
 * in bits 3-7, and an angle (lanes, 256 steps of a turn) or a radius
 * (circles, in 0.1 m) in bits 8-15.
 */
export const Telegraph = {
  None: 0,
  /** A circle around the entity (blast, slam) or at a hazard. */
  Circle: 1,
  /** A lane from the entity along the angle (charge, dash). */
  Lane: 2,
  /** A support pulse (shield, heal, summon) about to go off. */
  Aura: 3,
} as const;

/**
 * Per-spawn multipliers (the spawn director's difficulty curve and density
 * compensation). Health and damage are rounded to integers on the entity.
 */
export interface SpawnScale {
  readonly health?: number;
  readonly damage?: number;
  readonly xp?: number;
  /** An elite: x6 health, x1.5 damage, x5 XP, EntityFlag.Elite (on top of the multipliers above). */
  readonly elite?: boolean;
  /** The enemy it came out of (summons, splits): reported on entity.spawned. */
  readonly from?: number;
}

/**
 * The visible ground around a player, as distances from the player to the
 * edge of the screen at evenly spaced headings (index i is the heading
 * 2*pi*i/n, measured from +x toward +z). The spawn director spawns just
 * outside it, and the playtest counts what is inside it as "on screen".
 */
export interface ViewRules {
  readonly radii: readonly number[];
}

/**
 * Weapon behaviours (content mode). Survivor weapons fire by themselves:
 *  - `nova`: a burst that hits every enemy within `range`, when one is in range.
 *  - `bolt`: `count` projectiles at the nearest enemy within `range`, moving at `speed` m/s, passing through `pierce` enemies.
 *  - `orbit`: `count` blades circling at `range` m and `speed` rad/s; each blade hits an enemy at most every 8 ticks.
 * Arena weapons fire on Button.Fire along the player's aim (yaw):
 *  - `blaster`: `count` projectiles fanned over `spread` radians at `speed` m/s for `range` m.
 *  - `beam`: an instant hitscan to `range` m (stopped by pillars and walls); a room server resolves it with lag compensation.
 *  - `nova` (arena): a blast hitting every opponent within `range` m.
 */
export type WeaponKind = "nova" | "bolt" | "orbit" | "blaster" | "beam" | "cone" | "chain" | "aura" | "meteor" | "boomerang";

/** A weapon's numbers at one level (absolute, before passives). */
export interface WeaponLevelStats {
  readonly damage: number;
  readonly cooldownTicks: number;
  readonly range: number;
  readonly count: number;
  readonly speed: number;
  readonly pierce: number;
  readonly knockback: number;
  /** Cone: total angle, radians. */
  readonly spread: number;
}

export interface WeaponDef {
  readonly kind: WeaponKind;
  readonly damage: number;
  /** Ticks between shots (nova, bolt). Orbit ignores it. */
  readonly cooldownTicks: number;
  readonly range: number;
  readonly count: number;
  readonly speed: number;
  readonly pierce: number;
  /** m/s pushed into the enemy (divided by its mass). */
  readonly knockback: number;
  /** 1..15. */
  readonly maxLevel: number;
  /** Arena blaster: total fan angle of `count` projectiles, radians. Default 0. Cone: total angle of the sweep. */
  readonly spread?: number;
  /** Explicit numbers per level (index 0 is level 1). Without it, each level adds 25% damage, -6% cooldown, +1 count every 2 levels and +8% nova range. */
  readonly levels?: readonly WeaponLevelStats[];
  /** Meteor: blast radius, m (default 1.6). */
  readonly blast?: number;
  /** An evolution target: never offered on its own, only as an evolution. */
  readonly evolved?: boolean;
  /** Evolution: at max level, with passive `requires` (index into content.stats) taken, this weapon becomes weapon `into`. */
  readonly evolve?: { readonly into: number; readonly requires: number };
}

export type StatKind = "speed" | "maxHealth" | "magnet" | "might" | "haste" | "regen" | "armor" | "area" | "amount";

/**
 * A passive upgrade. Per level: speed and might multiply by (1 + step x level),
 * haste multiplies cooldowns by (1 - step x level) (floor 0.3), maxHealth and
 * magnet add step x level, regen heals step x level per second, armor removes
 * step x level from each contact hit (floor 1).
 */
export interface StatDef {
  readonly stat: StatKind;
  readonly step: number;
  /** 1..15. */
  readonly maxLevel: number;
}

export interface ProgressionRules {
  /** XP to reach level L+1 from L: xpBase + xpGrowth x (L - 1). */
  readonly xpBase: number;
  readonly xpGrowth: number;
  /** Base pickup (magnet) radius, m. */
  readonly magnet: number;
  /** Weapon slots per player (1..4). */
  readonly maxWeapons: number;
  /** Weapon index every player starts a run with, or -1. */
  readonly startWeapon: number;
  /** Most gems on the floor; past it XP goes straight to the killer. */
  readonly maxPickups: number;
  /** Card rerolls each player gets per run (Button.Reroll). */
  readonly rerolls: number;
  /** Curve exponent: XP to reach L+1 is xpBase + xpGrowth x (L - 1)^xpExponent. Default 1 (linear). */
  readonly xpExponent: number;
  /** Arena: the weapon indices every player carries in slots 1..4 (the loadout). Empty: `startWeapon` only. */
  readonly loadout: readonly number[];
  /** Co-op XP sharing (default: the collector only). */
  readonly xpShare: XpShare;
  /**
   * Critical hits: a hit on an enemy crits when critRoll(tick, enemy netId) < critChance,
   * dealing critMultiplier x damage. The roll is a fixed hash, so clients can mark crit numbers.
   */
  readonly critChance: number;
  readonly critMultiplier: number;
}

/**
 * Player ids from here up are server-side bots (seat fillers). They play
 * through the same sim; their arena beams resolve in the sim, never through
 * the room's lag compensation (a bot sees the present).
 */
export const BOT_PLAYER_BASE = 0xff00;

/**
 * Arena (shooter) mode: players aim with `yaw` and move in the world frame,
 * fire their selected loadout weapon on `Button.Fire`, hurt each other, die
 * and respawn at the spawn point farthest from their opponents.
 */
export interface ArenaRules {
  readonly enabled: boolean;
  /**
   * True on the authoritative side (room server, harness): projectiles,
   * hits, deaths, respawns and pickups happen. A predicting client sets it
   * false and predicts only its own movement, aim, weapon choice and cooldowns.
   */
  readonly authority: boolean;
  /**
   * True on a room server: human players' beams are resolved by the room's
   * lag-compensated rewind (`beamShot`, `applyBeamHit`), not in `step`.
   * Bots (`BOT_PLAYER_BASE` and up) always resolve in `step`.
   */
  readonly externalHitscan: boolean;
  /** Ticks a killed player waits before respawning. */
  readonly respawnTicks: number;
  /** Invulnerable ticks after a respawn (firing ends it early). */
  readonly spawnIframeTicks: number;
  /** Respawn points (x, z), m. Empty: the arena spawn. */
  readonly spawns: readonly (readonly [number, number])[];
  /** Health a killed player's dropped pickup restores (0: no drop). */
  readonly dropHeal: number;
  /** Ticks a dropped pickup stays on the floor. */
  readonly pickupTicks: number;
}

export interface CoopRules {
  /** Ticks a downed player bleeds before they are out (dead until `respawnDead`). */
  readonly downedTicks: number;
  /** Ticks a teammate must stand within `reviveRadius` to revive. */
  readonly reviveTicks: number;
  readonly reviveRadius: number;
  /** Health after a revive, as a fraction of max. */
  readonly reviveHealth: number;
  /** Invulnerable ticks after a revive or a respawn. */
  readonly iframeTicks: number;
  /** Ticks a killed enemy stays as a corpse (so clients see it die). */
  readonly corpseTicks: number;
  /** Dash: ticks, speed multiplier, cooldown ticks, input buffer ticks. */
  readonly dashTicks: number;
  readonly dashSpeed: number;
  readonly dashCooldownTicks: number;
  readonly dashBufferTicks: number;
  /** Ticks a player is immune to contact damage after taking a contact hit (hit i-frames). */
  readonly hitIframeTicks: number;
  /** Pause the whole sim while the only player in the world has upgrade cards open. */
  readonly pauseSolo: boolean;
  /**
   * Prediction worlds hold only their own character, so they cannot count
   * players: they take EntityFlag.Solo from snapshots instead of setting it.
   * The adapter sets this on client worlds.
   */
  readonly soloFromFlag: boolean;
  /** Co-op: opening cards knocks enemies back within this radius (m) and grants these i-frame ticks. */
  readonly choicePulseRadius: number;
  readonly choicePulseIframeTicks: number;
  /** A teammate who revives someone gets a buff for this many ticks (0: none; max 4095). */
  readonly reviveBuffTicks: number;
  /** While buffed: damage multiplier and move speed multiplier. */
  readonly reviveBuffMight: number;
  readonly reviveBuffSpeed: number;
  /** A downed player crawls at this fraction of run speed (0: they cannot move). */
  readonly crawlSpeed: number;
  /**
   * Free self-revives per player per run (0..15): Sprint while downed stands
   * you up (after `selfReviveDelayTicks`), and an unused one is spent by
   * itself when the downed timer runs out. Stored in Game.bleed bits 12..15.
   */
  readonly selfRevives: number;
  readonly selfReviveDelayTicks: number;
  /**
   * Ticks a dead (out) player waits before coming back beside a teammate who
   * is up (0: out until `respawnDead`). Counted down in Game.bleed bits 0..11.
   */
  readonly respawnTicks: number;
  /** Getting up (self-revive or respawn) shoves enemies within this radius, m (0: none). */
  readonly risePulseRadius: number;
}

/**
 * Game content: when `weapons` is non-empty the world runs in content mode
 * (auto-firing weapons, XP gems, level-ups, co-op downed and revive, dash)
 * instead of the week-2 arena rules (Fire = pulse, respawn on death).
 */
export interface ContentConfig {
  readonly enemyTypes?: readonly EnemyTypeDef[];
  readonly weapons?: readonly WeaponDef[];
  readonly stats?: readonly StatDef[];
  readonly progression?: Partial<ProgressionRules>;
  readonly coop?: Partial<CoopRules>;
  /** Arena (shooter) mode; off unless `enabled`. */
  readonly arena?: Partial<ArenaRules>;
  readonly view?: ViewRules;
  /** Special pickups (heals, vacuums, bombs, chests). */
  readonly pickups?: readonly PickupTypeDef[];
  /** Loot: the special pickups elites and bosses drop (indices into pickups; -1 none). */
  readonly loot?: { readonly chest: number; readonly heal: number; readonly vacuum: number; readonly bossChest?: number };
  /** Gems on the floor above this merge into the nearest gem instead of a new one (default 300). */
  readonly mergeGemsAbove?: number;
  /** Playable characters (keepers); empty: everyone starts with `progression.startWeapon`. At most 15. */
  readonly characters?: readonly CharacterDef[];
}

export interface ResolvedContent {
  readonly enabled: boolean;
  readonly enemyTypes: readonly EnemyTypeDef[];
  readonly weapons: readonly WeaponDef[];
  readonly stats: readonly StatDef[];
  readonly progression: ProgressionRules;
  readonly coop: CoopRules;
  readonly arena: ArenaRules;
  readonly view: ViewRules;
  readonly pickups: readonly PickupTypeDef[];
  readonly loot: { readonly chest: number; readonly heal: number; readonly vacuum: number; readonly bossChest?: number };
  readonly mergeGemsAbove: number;
  readonly characters: readonly CharacterDef[];
}

export interface SimConfig {
  /** Fixed tick rate in Hz. Default `DEFAULT_TICK_RATE`. */
  readonly tickRate?: number;
  /** Seed for the sim's PRNG (u32). Default 1. */
  readonly seed?: number;
  /** Hard cap on live entities. Default 8192. */
  readonly maxEntities?: number;
  readonly arena?: Partial<ArenaConfig>;
  readonly player?: Partial<PlayerRules>;
  readonly enemies?: Partial<EnemyRules>;
  readonly content?: ContentConfig;
}

export interface ResolvedSimConfig {
  readonly tickRate: number;
  readonly seed: number;
  readonly maxEntities: number;
  readonly arena: ArenaConfig;
  readonly player: PlayerRules;
  readonly enemies: EnemyRules;
  readonly content: ResolvedContent;
}

/**
 * A simulation world. Opaque on purpose: callers read it through the
 * functions in this package, never through ECS or Rapier handles.
 */
export interface SimWorld {
  /** Ticks stepped so far. */
  readonly tick: number;
  readonly tickRate: number;
  /** Seconds per tick, 1 / tickRate. */
  readonly dt: number;
  readonly config: ResolvedSimConfig;
}

/** Things that happened during one step, in the order they happened. */
export type SimEvent =
  | { readonly type: "player.joined"; readonly playerId: PlayerId; readonly netId: NetId }
  | { readonly type: "player.left"; readonly playerId: PlayerId; readonly netId: NetId }
  | {
      readonly type: "player.hit";
      readonly playerId: PlayerId;
      readonly netId: NetId;
      readonly by: NetId;
      readonly damage: number;
      readonly health: number;
      /** What hit: a touch, or a telegraphed attack (charge, blast, boss pattern, enemy projectile). Default "contact". */
      readonly source?: HitSource;
      /** The enemy type that hit, when `by` is not an enemy (a shot or a hazard it left). */
      readonly enemyType?: number;
    }
  | { readonly type: "player.died"; readonly playerId: PlayerId; readonly netId: NetId }
  /** Arena: a player was killed; `by` is the player credited (0: no one). */
  | { readonly type: "player.killed"; readonly playerId: PlayerId; readonly netId: NetId; readonly by: PlayerId }
  /** Arena: a player fired weapon slot `slot` (0..3). */
  | { readonly type: "player.shot"; readonly playerId: PlayerId; readonly netId: NetId; readonly slot: number }
  | { readonly type: "player.respawned"; readonly playerId: PlayerId; readonly netId: NetId }
  | { readonly type: "player.pulse"; readonly playerId: PlayerId; readonly netId: NetId }
  | {
      readonly type: "enemy.killed";
      readonly netId: NetId;
      /** The player whose weapon landed the kill (0 if none). */
      readonly by: PlayerId;
      /** Enemy type index (0 in the arena). */
      readonly enemyType: number;
      readonly boss: boolean;
      /** An elite (gold rim) died. */
      readonly elite?: boolean;
    }
  | { readonly type: "player.downed"; readonly playerId: PlayerId; readonly netId: NetId }
  | { readonly type: "player.revived"; readonly playerId: PlayerId; readonly netId: NetId; readonly by: PlayerId }
  | { readonly type: "player.levelup"; readonly playerId: PlayerId; readonly netId: NetId; readonly level: number }
  | { readonly type: "player.upgraded"; readonly playerId: PlayerId; readonly netId: NetId; readonly upgrade: number; readonly evolved?: boolean }
  | { readonly type: "player.collected"; readonly playerId: PlayerId; readonly netId: NetId; readonly effect: PickupEffect }
  | {
      readonly type: "entity.spawned";
      readonly netId: NetId;
      readonly kind: EntityKindId;
      /** Spawned out of another enemy (a summon or a split), so it may appear on screen. */
      readonly from?: NetId;
    }
  | { readonly type: "entity.removed"; readonly netId: NetId; readonly kind: EntityKindId };

export interface StepResult {
  /** The tick number this step produced (world.tick after the step). */
  readonly tick: number;
  readonly events: readonly SimEvent[];
}

/**
 * One entity's networked state. Every field is an integer: positions and
 * velocities in fixed point (`POSITION_SCALE`, `VELOCITY_SCALE`), yaw as a
 * u16 turn. The sim keeps its own state on this grid at every tick
 * boundary, so capture → apply is lossless.
 */
export interface EntityState {
  netId: NetId;
  kind: EntityKindId;
  /** Owning player, or 0. */
  owner: PlayerId;
  px: number;
  py: number;
  pz: number;
  vx: number;
  vy: number;
  vz: number;
  yaw: number;
  health: number;
  /** `EntityFlag` bits. */
  flags: number;
  /** Players: last input seq processed (the reconciliation ack). Others: 0. */
  ack: number;
  /** Players: ticks until Fire is ready. Enemies: ticks until next contact. */
  cooldown: number;
  /** Players: last buttons held (edge detection). Others: 0. */
  buttons: number;
  /** Players: coyote/jump-buffer timers packed (coyote | buffer << 8). Others: 0. */
  timers: number;
  /** Enemies: type index. Pickups: gem tier. Projectiles: weapon index. Players: cosmetic id. */
  type: number;
  /** Pickups: XP value. Projectiles: damage. */
  value: number;
  /** Players: level (1..). Projectiles: pierce left. */
  level: number;
  /** Players: XP toward the next level. Projectiles: last enemy hit (netId). */
  xp: number;
  /** Players: 4 weapon slots, 8 bits each: (weapon index + 1) | level << 4. */
  weapons: number;
  /** Players: 4 weapon cooldowns in ticks, 8 bits each. */
  wcd: number;
  /** Players: up to 6 passive stat levels, 4 bits each. */
  stats: number;
  /** Players: 3 offered upgrades (index + 1), 8 bits each, then pending level-ups in bits 24..31. */
  choices: number;
  /** Players: downed ticks left (co-op). */
  bleed: number;
  /** Players: revive progress ticks while downed. */
  revive: number;
  /** Players: invulnerable ticks left. */
  iframes: number;
  /** Players: dash ticks left | cooldown << 8 | buffered press << 16. */
  dash: number;
}

/** A whole world's networked state at one tick. Entities sorted by netId. */
export interface SimState {
  tick: number;
  /** PRNG state (u32). */
  rng: number;
  /** Next NetId to assign. */
  nextNetId: number;
  /** Enemies killed so far (game-rules counter). */
  kills: number;
  entities: EntityState[];
}

/** One player as game logic sees it (`listPlayers`). */
export interface PlayerSummary {
  readonly playerId: PlayerId;
  readonly netId: NetId;
  readonly x: number;
  readonly y: number;
  readonly z: number;
  readonly health: number;
  readonly maxHealth: number;
  readonly level: number;
  /** Not downed and not dead. */
  readonly up: boolean;
  readonly downed: boolean;
  readonly dead: boolean;
  /** Arena: the selected loadout slot (0..3). */
  readonly slot: number;
  /** The keeper (character) index; 0 when the game declares none. */
  readonly keeper: number;
  /** A revive buff is running. */
  readonly buffed: boolean;
  /** Free self-revives left this run (coop.selfRevives). */
  readonly selfRevives: number;
}

/**
 * Dense, renderer-friendly arrays for the current tick, plus the previous
 * tick's transform for interpolation (`alpha` from `FixedStepper`). Valid
 * until the next `step` or `applyState` on the same world.
 */
export interface RenderView {
  readonly tick: number;
  readonly count: number;
  readonly netId: Uint32Array;
  readonly kind: Uint8Array;
  readonly owner: Uint16Array;
  readonly health: Uint16Array;
  readonly flags: Uint8Array;
  readonly x: Float32Array;
  readonly y: Float32Array;
  readonly z: Float32Array;
  readonly yaw: Float32Array;
  readonly prevX: Float32Array;
  readonly prevY: Float32Array;
  readonly prevZ: Float32Array;
  readonly prevYaw: Float32Array;
}

/** Result of advancing a `FixedStepper` by wall-clock time. */
export interface StepperAdvance {
  /** Fixed ticks to run now (0..maxTicksPerAdvance). */
  readonly ticks: number;
  /** Interpolation factor 0..1 between the last two ticks, for rendering. */
  readonly alpha: number;
  /** Ticks dropped because the caller fell too far behind (spiral-of-death guard). */
  readonly dropped: number;
}
```

## Part 5: physics types (src/physics/types.ts)

```ts
import type { Vec3 } from "../api.js";

/** A stable id for one body in a PhysicsWorld (u32, assigned in creation order, never reused). */
export type BodyId = number;
/** A stable id for one joint. */
export type JointId = number;
/** Quaternion [x, y, z, w]. */
export type Quat = readonly [x: number, y: number, z: number, w: number];

export type BodyType = "dynamic" | "kinematic" | "static";

/** Collision shapes. Capsules and cylinders stand along +y. */
export type ShapeDesc =
  | { readonly box: Vec3 }
  | { readonly sphere: number }
  | { readonly capsule: readonly [halfHeight: number, radius: number] }
  | { readonly cylinder: readonly [halfHeight: number, radius: number] };

export interface BodyDesc {
  readonly type: BodyType;
  readonly shape: ShapeDesc;
  readonly position?: Vec3;
  readonly rotation?: Quat;
  /** Total mass, kg. Overrides `density`. */
  readonly mass?: number;
  /** kg/m³. Default 1. */
  readonly density?: number;
  /** Default 0.5. */
  readonly friction?: number;
  /** 0 (dead) to 1 (perfect bounce). Default 0. */
  readonly restitution?: number;
  readonly linearDamping?: number;
  readonly angularDamping?: number;
  /** Default 1. */
  readonly gravityScale?: number;
  /** One `Layer` bit. Default `Layer.Prop`. */
  readonly layer?: number;
  /** `Layer` bits this body collides with. Default every layer. */
  readonly mask?: number;
  /** A trigger volume: reports enter and exit, never pushes anything. */
  readonly sensor?: boolean;
  /** Continuous collision detection: fast bodies (projectiles) never tunnel through thin walls. */
  readonly ccd?: boolean;
  /** Keep the body upright (no rotation from contacts). */
  readonly lockRotations?: boolean;
  /** Initial velocities. */
  readonly linearVelocity?: Vec3;
  readonly angularVelocity?: Vec3;
  /** Any number the game wants back from queries and events (e.g. a NetId). Default 0. */
  readonly userData?: number;
}

export type PhysicsEventType = "contact.start" | "contact.end" | "trigger.enter" | "trigger.exit";

/** A contact or trigger change during one step. `a < b`; for triggers one of them is the sensor. */
export interface PhysicsEvent {
  readonly type: PhysicsEventType;
  readonly a: BodyId;
  readonly b: BodyId;
}

export interface RayHit {
  readonly body: BodyId;
  readonly point: Vec3;
  readonly normal: Vec3;
  readonly distance: number;
}

export interface ShapeHit {
  readonly body: BodyId;
  /** Distance travelled along the cast direction before touching. */
  readonly distance: number;
  /** Contact point on the hit body. */
  readonly point: Vec3;
  /** Surface normal of the hit body at the contact. */
  readonly normal: Vec3;
}

export interface QueryOptions {
  /** `Layer` bits to look at. Default every layer. */
  readonly mask?: number;
  /** Bodies to ignore (e.g. the shooter). */
  readonly exclude?: readonly BodyId[];
  /** Include trigger volumes. Default false. */
  readonly includeSensors?: boolean;
}

export type JointKind = "fixed" | "ball" | "hinge" | "slider";

export interface JointDesc {
  readonly kind: JointKind;
  readonly a: BodyId;
  readonly b: BodyId;
  /** Anchor in body a's local frame. Default origin. */
  readonly anchorA?: Vec3;
  /** Anchor in body b's local frame. Default origin. */
  readonly anchorB?: Vec3;
  /** Hinge or slider axis (local). Default +y. */
  readonly axis?: Vec3;
}

export interface KnockbackOptions {
  /** Upward velocity added, m/s. Default 0. */
  readonly lift?: number;
  /** Divide the velocity change by the body's mass (heavy bodies move less). Default false: every mass gets `strength` m/s. */
  readonly byMass?: boolean;
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------ characters

/** A kinematic character (capsule on Rapier's character controller). All fields optional except where noted. */
export interface CharacterDesc {
  readonly position: Vec3;
  readonly radius?: number;
  /** Half-height of the capsule's cylinder, m. */
  readonly halfHeight?: number;
  /** Default `Layer.Player`. */
  readonly layer?: number;
  /** Layers the character collides with. Default Level | Prop | Enemy | Player | Trigger (triggers report it, never block it). */
  readonly mask?: number;
  /** Controller skin, m. Default 0.02. */
  readonly offset?: number;
  /** Steepest walkable slope, degrees. Default 45. */
  readonly maxSlopeClimb?: number;
  /** Slopes steeper than this slide the character down, degrees. Default 50. */
  readonly minSlopeSlide?: number;
  /** Auto-step height and minimum free width on top, m. Height 0 disables steps. Default 0.35 / 0.2. */
  readonly stepHeight?: number;
  readonly stepWidth?: number;
  /** Climb steps onto dynamic bodies too. Default false. */
  readonly stepOverDynamic?: boolean;
  /** Keep contact with the ground going down small drops, m. 0 disables. Default 0.3. */
  readonly snapToGround?: number;
  /** Top ground speed, m/s. Default 6. */
  readonly maxSpeed?: number;
  /** Ground acceleration toward the stick and deceleration with no stick, m/s². Default 60 / 80. */
  readonly groundAccel?: number;
  readonly groundDecel?: number;
  /** Air control: acceleration and deceleration in the air, m/s². Default 18 / 4. */
  readonly airAccel?: number;
  readonly airDecel?: number;
  /** Jump take-off speed, m/s. Default 7. */
  readonly jumpVelocity?: number;
  /** Releasing jump while rising multiplies upward speed by this (variable jump height). 1 disables. Default 0.45. */
  readonly jumpCut?: number;
  /** Multiplies the world's gravity. Default 1. */
  readonly gravityScale?: number;
  /** Fastest fall, m/s. Default 40. */
  readonly terminalVelocity?: number;
  /** Ticks after leaving a ledge during which a jump still works. Default 5. */
  readonly coyoteTicks?: number;
  /** Ticks a jump press is remembered before landing. Default 5. */
  readonly jumpBufferTicks?: number;
  /** Dash: duration in ticks (0 disables), speed m/s, cooldown ticks, input buffer ticks, invulnerable while dashing. */
  readonly dashTicks?: number;
  readonly dashSpeed?: number;
  readonly dashCooldownTicks?: number;
  readonly dashBufferTicks?: number;
  readonly dashInvulnerable?: boolean;
  /** Push dynamic bodies the character walks into. Default true. */
  readonly pushBodies?: boolean;
  /** Mass used when pushing, kg. Default 80. */
  readonly mass?: number;
  readonly userData?: number;
}

export type ResolvedCharacterDesc = Required<Omit<CharacterDesc, "position">> & { readonly position: Vec3 };

/** One tick of character input. Move is in world space (x right, z toward the camera), -1..1. */
export interface CharacterInput {
  readonly moveX: number;
  readonly moveZ: number;
  /** Held. Pressed edges are found inside the motor. */
  readonly jump?: boolean;
  readonly dash?: boolean;
}

/** A character's whole motor state: plain numbers, serialized in snapshots. */
export interface CharacterState {
  x: number;
  y: number;
  z: number;
  vx: number;
  vy: number;
  vz: number;
  grounded: boolean;
  /** Coyote ticks left. */
  coyote: number;
  /** Buffered jump ticks left. */
  jumpBuffer: number;
  /** Rising from a jump that can still be cut. */
  jumping: boolean;
  dashTicks: number;
  dashCooldown: number;
  dashBuffer: number;
  dashX: number;
  dashZ: number;
  /** Last horizontal move direction (dash with no stick goes this way). Starts facing -z. */
  facingX: number;
  facingZ: number;
  invulnerable: boolean;
  /** Last held buttons: 1 jump, 2 dash. */
  buttons: number;
  groundNormalX: number;
  groundNormalY: number;
  groundNormalZ: number;
}

export interface CharacterReport {
  readonly id: BodyId;
  readonly grounded: boolean;
  readonly landed: boolean;
  readonly jumped: boolean;
  readonly dashed: boolean;
  readonly hitCeiling: boolean;
  readonly groundNormal: Vec3;
}

export interface PhysicsStepResult {
  /** world tick after the step. */
  readonly tick: number;
  readonly events: readonly PhysicsEvent[];
  /** One report per character, in BodyId order. */
  readonly characters: readonly CharacterReport[];
}
```
